questions.prompt: Assume int is 4 bytes and row-major layout. What is the byte offset of a[2][1] in int a[4][3], from a[0][0]?
questions.explanation: The linear element offset is 2*3+1=7. At four bytes per int, the byte offset is 7*4=28.

questions.prompt: For int a[7]={0}; in the same scope, what does sizeof(a)/sizeof(a[0]) evaluate to?
questions.explanation: sizeof(a) includes all seven int elements; sizeof(a[0]) is one int. Their ratio gives the element count.

questions.prompt: For char text[]="GATE"; what value does sizeof(text) return?
questions.explanation: The array stores four visible characters plus the terminating null character, so sizeof reports five bytes.

questions.prompt: For char text[]="GATE"; what does strlen(text) return before modification?
questions.explanation: strlen counts characters up to but excluding the null terminator.

questions.prompt: Let int a[9]; int *p=&a[2] and int *q=&a[8]. What is q-p?
questions.explanation: Pointer subtraction for elements of the same array returns their element-index difference: 8-2=6.

questions.prompt: For int a[4]; int *p=&a[3]; which operation is defined?
options: Forming p+1 as a one-past pointer
answer: Forming p+1 as a one-past pointer
questions.explanation: C permits a pointer one past an array end for comparison or subtraction, but it cannot be dereferenced or advanced farther.

questions.prompt: In a function parameter declaration void f(int values[20]), what type does values have inside f?
answer: int *
questions.explanation: Array parameters are adjusted to pointer parameters. The function receives an int pointer; the bound 20 does not automatically enforce a runtime length.

questions.prompt: A function void inc(int x) executes x=x+1. The caller passes variable n. What is guaranteed about n after the call?
options: The call does not modify n through x
The result depends on stack layout
answer: The call does not modify n through x
questions.explanation: C passes the scalar value by value. The function changes its local parameter copy, not the caller object.

questions.prompt: A block-scope static int counter starts without an initializer and is incremented once per call. What is its value after 9 calls?
questions.explanation: A static-storage object is zero-initialized once and retains its value between calls. Nine increments produce 9.

questions.prompt: What initial value does a file-scope int object without an explicit initializer have?
options: The value of the first input read
questions.explanation: Objects with static storage duration are zero-initialized when no initializer is provided.

questions.prompt: A function declares static int calls; and increments calls every invocation. What happens to calls between invocations?
options: Its value is retained for the program duration
It is recreated with value zero on every call
It becomes a global variable visible to all translation units
It is stored in the caller stack frame
answer: Its value is retained for the program duration
questions.explanation: A block-scope static object has static storage duration. Its name remains block-scoped, but its stored value persists across calls.

questions.prompt: What is the status of reading an uninitialized automatic int local variable?
options: It has an indeterminate value and using it can have undefined behavior
It is guaranteed to be zero
It is guaranteed to equal the last value at that stack address
It is implementation-defined but always safe
answer: It has an indeterminate value and using it can have undefined behavior
questions.explanation: An automatic object without an initializer is not zero-initialized. Evaluating its indeterminate value is not a portable operation.

questions.prompt: At file scope, what does extern int total; normally declare?
options: An object defined elsewhere without defining storage here
answer: An object defined elsewhere without defining storage here
questions.explanation: A file-scope extern declaration refers to an externally linked object. Without an initializer, it is a declaration rather than a tentative definition.

questions.prompt: What does static on a file-scope function declaration specify?
options: Internal linkage within that translation unit
External linkage across the whole program
Automatic storage duration for each call
answer: Internal linkage within that translation unit
questions.explanation: A file-scope static function name is not visible to other translation units; static changes linkage in this context.

questions.prompt: Given int a[3], b[3]; what does the statement a=b; do in standard C?
options: It violates a constraint because arrays are not assignable
It copies the address of b
answer: It violates a constraint because arrays are not assignable
questions.explanation: Array objects are not modifiable lvalues and cannot be assigned wholesale. Elements must be copied individually or through a library routine.

questions.prompt: For int a[2][5], what is the type of a+1 after array conversion?
options: Pointer to an array of 5 int
Pointer to an array of 2 int
answer: Pointer to an array of 5 int
questions.explanation: The outer array decays to a pointer to its first row. Each row has type int[5], so adding one advances by one row.

questions.prompt: Inside a function, sizeof applied to a parameter declared int x[] yields what?
options: The size of an int pointer
The total size of the caller array
The size of the first int
answer: The size of an int pointer
questions.explanation: The parameter is adjusted to int *x. sizeof measures that pointer object; the array length must be passed separately.

questions.prompt: For char s[4]="GATE"; which statement is correct?
options: The initializer cannot fit because the null terminator needs a fifth element
It is valid and stores the complete string including terminator
It silently truncates the last character
answer: The initializer cannot fit because the null terminator needs a fifth element
questions.explanation: The string literal has five char elements including its terminator. An array of four cannot hold the full initializer as written.

questions.prompt: Which printf conversion is intended for a value of type size_t returned by sizeof?
answer: %zu
questions.explanation: sizeof has type size_t. The z length modifier with u is the matching standard conversion for an unsigned integer type such as size_t.

questions.prompt: For int a[]={3,5,8,12}; int *p=a; what value does p[2] designate?
questions.explanation: p[2] is *(p+2). Since p points to a[0], it selects a[2], whose value is 8.

questions.prompt: For int a[4]; int *p=&a[1]; which expression denotes the address of a[3]?
questions.explanation: Starting at a[1], advancing the pointer by two elements yields a[3].

questions.prompt: For char *p="abc";, which operation has undefined behavior?
options: Passing p to a function taking const char *
answer: Attempting to modify p[0]
questions.explanation: A string literal is not modifiable. Reading its characters is allowed, but writing through p has undefined behavior.

questions.prompt: For int a[3]={1,2}; what value is stored in a[2]?
questions.explanation: Aggregate initialization supplies zero values for array elements omitted from the initializer list.

questions.prompt: Which C function counts characters in a null-terminated string s, excluding its terminator?
answer: strlen(s)
questions.explanation: strlen counts characters before the first null byte. sizeof may measure an array or just a pointer, depending on context.

questions.prompt: For char word[]="net"; what is sizeof(word)?
questions.explanation: The array contains n, e, t, and a terminating null character, so it has four char elements.

questions.prompt: For int a[5], what is the result of 2[a]?
answer: The same element as a[2]
questions.explanation: C defines a[i] as *(a+i). Pointer addition is commutative, so 2[a] is equivalent to a[2], though it is unusual style.

questions.prompt: In a function parameter written int x[static 8], what does static require of each call?
options: The argument provides access to at least eight int elements
The function allocates eight ints automatically
The argument has static storage duration
The parameter becomes a global array
answer: The argument provides access to at least eight int elements
questions.explanation: The static array-parameter qualifier expresses a minimum accessible element count; it does not allocate storage.

questions.prompt: In the declaration int (*p)[6], what does p point to?
options: An array of six int pointers
answer: An array of six int
questions.explanation: Parentheses make p a pointer to an array of six int, rather than an array of pointers.

questions.prompt: Which declaration is an array of four pointers to char?
answer: char *names[4];
questions.explanation: Array subscripting binds more tightly than unary *, so names is an array whose elements are char pointers.

questions.prompt: Assume 8-bit unsigned char. What value results from unsigned char x=250; x+=10; ?
questions.explanation: The compound assignment converts the sum back to an 8-bit unsigned type. 260 modulo 256 is 4.

questions.prompt: Assume 32-bit unsigned int. What value does 0u-1u produce?
questions.explanation: Unsigned arithmetic is modulo 2^32, so zero minus one yields 2^32-1.

questions.prompt: Assume 32-bit signed int with x=INT_MAX. What happens when x is incremented?
options: The behavior is undefined due to signed overflow
It is guaranteed to wrap to INT_MIN
answer: The behavior is undefined due to signed overflow
questions.explanation: C does not define signed overflow. Hardware wraparound does not make the expression portable.

questions.prompt: Assume unsigned char is 8 bits and int can represent 0 through 255. What value does the expression (unsigned char)255 + 1 have before assignment to any narrower object?
questions.explanation: The unsigned char operand is promoted to int because int represents its full range. The addition therefore occurs as int and yields 256; it does not wrap at 8 bits.

questions.prompt: For unsigned int x, which expression tests whether its least significant bit is set?
questions.explanation: Bitwise AND with one isolates the low bit. Comparing that masked result with zero tests whether it is set.

questions.prompt: Given int a[]={4,9,13}; int *p=a; then execute int first=*p++; followed by int second=*p; what values are stored in first and second?
answer: 4 and 9
questions.explanation: Each statement is a separate full expression. The first reads a[0] and advances p; the next reads a[1], so the values are 4 and 9.

questions.prompt: If p points to a modifiable int, what does (*p)++ do?
options: Increment the pointer by one byte
answer: Increment the pointed-to int
questions.explanation: Parentheses make indirection occur first, so postfix increment applies to the int object reached through p.

questions.prompt: Which uses of an array expression avoid array-to-pointer conversion?
options: Passing a as an int * argument
answer: sizeof a
questions.explanation: The operand of sizeof is an exception to array conversion when it is not a variable-length array type. Other listed contexts use the array as a pointer.

questions.prompt: For int a[4]; int *p=&a[0]; int *q=&a[3]; what is q-p?
questions.explanation: Pointer subtraction within one array is measured in elements. The index difference is 3, independent of int byte size.

questions.prompt: Which operation on int a[5] is defined when p=&a[4]?
answer: Compare p+1 with a+5
questions.explanation: p+1 is the one-past pointer and equals a+5. It may be formed but not dereferenced or advanced farther.

questions.prompt: Which declaration denotes a pointer to a function taking int and returning int?
answer: int (*fp)(int);
questions.explanation: Parentheses bind the pointer declarator to fp before the function parameter list. Without parentheses, int *fp(int) declares a function returning int pointer.

questions.prompt: What does const int *p allow?
options: Changing p to point elsewhere but not modifying the int through p
Modifying p but not changing the int value
Neither changing p nor modifying the int
Changing both p and the int freely
answer: Changing p to point elsewhere but not modifying the int through p
questions.explanation: The pointed-to type is const-qualified through this access path, but p itself is not const and may be reassigned.

questions.prompt: What does int * const p mean?
options: p cannot be reassigned, but the pointed-to int may be modified
p points to a const int
Both p and the int are const
answer: p cannot be reassigned, but the pointed-to int may be modified
questions.explanation: The const qualifier applies to the pointer object itself. It does not qualify the int that p points to.

questions.prompt: What guarantee does volatile provide by itself?
options: It does not make accesses atomic or thread-safe
answer: It does not make accesses atomic or thread-safe
questions.explanation: volatile affects optimization assumptions about accesses but is not an atomicity or synchronization mechanism.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes restrict in C99 and later?
options: It is an aliasing promise about access to an object through a pointer
It means the pointer cannot be null
It makes the pointed-to object const
It requests that the pointer be stored in a register
answer: It is an aliasing promise about access to an object through a pointer
questions.explanation: restrict communicates a restricted access association for an object during a block execution. Violating that promise can yield undefined behavior.

questions.prompt: Assume struct S { char c; int x; } with int alignment 4 and natural padding. What is sizeof(struct S)?
questions.explanation: c uses byte 0; padding aligns x at offset 4; the int ends at offset 8. Struct size is rounded to its maximum member alignment, four.

questions.prompt: Why may memcmp on two structures report different bytes even when their members compare equal?
options: C stores a pointer in every structure
The structures must have different types
answer: Padding bytes may differ
questions.explanation: Padding can be part of the object representation without being a member value. Member-wise comparison avoids relying on unspecified padding bytes.

questions.prompt: For a union with members int i and char c, which is true about their storage?
options: The members overlap and begin at the same address
The union stores both in separate consecutive areas
Its size is always the sum of member sizes
Only the first member can ever be selected
answer: The members overlap and begin at the same address
questions.explanation: Union members share storage. The union has enough size and alignment for its largest member, rather than adding all member sizes.

questions.prompt: An enum is declared enum E {P=4, Q, R=9, S}; what value does S have?
questions.explanation: An enumerator without an explicit value is one greater than its predecessor. R is 9, so S is 10.

questions.prompt: Which statements about C structure and union objects are correct?
options: Compatible structures may be assigned as whole values
A structure may contain padding between members
All structure types are compared by memcmp
answer: Compatible structures may be assigned as whole values
Union members share overlapping storage
A structure may contain padding between members
questions.explanation: Structure assignment copies compatible structure values. Union members overlap in storage, and implementations may insert padding between structure members; bytewise comparison can therefore differ even when member values match.

questions.prompt: Which pointer type may inspect the object representation of an arbitrary object byte by byte?
options: A pointer to void after direct dereference
answer: A pointer to character type
questions.explanation: Character-type lvalues are allowed to inspect object representation. A void pointer must be converted to an object pointer type before dereferencing.

questions.prompt: What can happen when an object is accessed through an incompatible pointer type, outside specified exceptions?
options: It can violate effective-type rules and cause undefined behavior
The compiler always converts the representation safely
The object is copied to a temporary of the new type
It is safe whenever pointer sizes match
answer: It can violate effective-type rules and cause undefined behavior
questions.explanation: C restricts access to object storage through compatible types, with specified exceptions such as character types.

questions.prompt: Which statement about function pointers is correct?
options: A function pointer can be called with arguments matching its function type
A function pointer can be dereferenced to read machine code bytes portably
All object pointers and function pointers must have identical representations
A function pointer is an array of instructions
answer: A function pointer can be called with arguments matching its function type
questions.explanation: A function pointer designates a function and may be invoked through a compatible function type. Its representation need not match object pointers.

questions.prompt: Which declarations can represent a pointer to an array of five int?
answer: typedef int Row[5]; Row *p;
questions.explanation: Both the parenthesized declarator and the typedef form declare a pointer to an array of five int. An array of pointers and a pointer-to-pointer are different types.

questions.prompt: What does p->member mean for a pointer p to a structure object?
answer: (*p).member
questions.explanation: The arrow operator is equivalent to first dereferencing p, then selecting the named structure member.

questions.prompt: Evaluate 0x35u & 0x0Fu and give its decimal value.
questions.explanation: The mask keeps the low four bits of 0x35; 0101 in binary is decimal 5.

questions.prompt: Evaluate 0x35u ^ 0x0Fu and give the hexadecimal result.
questions.explanation: Hexadecimal XOR gives 0x35 XOR 0x0F = 0x3A because only corresponding equal bits become zero.

questions.prompt: Assume 32-bit unsigned int. What is the value of 1u << 5?
questions.explanation: Left-shifting unsigned one by five positions gives 2^5, which is 32.

questions.prompt: For a 32-bit unsigned int, which shift count makes x << count undefined?
questions.explanation: The shift count must be less than the width of the promoted left operand. A count of 32 is invalid for a 32-bit value.

questions.prompt: In C17, what can be concluded about right-shifting a negative signed integer?
options: It is always a logical shift
It is always division rounded toward zero
It is undefined on every implementation
answer: The result is implementation-defined
questions.explanation: C17 leaves right shift of a negative signed value implementation-defined. Portable code should not assume a particular sign-extension result.

questions.prompt: A function int inc(int x) returns x+1. If int (*fp)(int)=inc; what value does fp(6) return?
questions.explanation: fp stores a pointer to a function with compatible parameter and result types. Calling fp(6) invokes inc with 6 and returns 6+1=7.

questions.prompt: What is sizeof(int[3]) in bytes when sizeof(int) is 4?
questions.explanation: The type is an array of three int objects. Its size is 3*4=12 bytes.

questions.prompt: A variable-length array int a[n] has a run-time bound n. When is sizeof(a) determined?
options: At run time from the value of n
It is not permitted for a VLA
answer: At run time from the value of n
questions.explanation: A variable-length array has a bound evaluated at run time, and sizeof on its VLA type reflects that bound.

questions.prompt: Which type may control a switch statement in C after integer promotions?
answer: An integer type
questions.explanation: The controlling expression must have integer type after the permitted integer promotions.

questions.prompt: A break statement is inside a switch that itself is inside a while loop. What does break exit?
options: Both the switch and while loop
The current while iteration and then the switch
answer: The switch only
questions.explanation: break exits only the innermost enclosing switch or loop. Execution continues after the switch, still within the while body.

questions.prompt: In a for loop, where does continue transfer control?
options: To the iteration expression, then the next condition check
To the loop body start without checking the condition
answer: To the iteration expression, then the next condition check
questions.explanation: For a for loop, continue executes the iteration expression before evaluating the condition for the next iteration.

questions.prompt: What is guaranteed about sizeof(char) in C?
options: It is implementation-defined and may be zero
answer: It equals 1
questions.explanation: sizeof measures in C bytes, and a char always occupies exactly one such byte. A byte may have more than eight bits.

questions.prompt: What does CHAR_BIT from limits.h specify?
options: The number of bits in a byte
The number of bytes in an int
The number of bits in a pointer
The maximum number of chars in a string
answer: The number of bits in a byte
questions.explanation: CHAR_BIT defines how many bits are in one C byte; the standard does not require every byte to have exactly eight bits.

questions.prompt: Which statement about null pointers is guaranteed by C?
options: A null pointer compares unequal to every pointer to an object or function
A null pointer is represented by all zero bits
A null pointer always has type int *
A null pointer can be dereferenced to obtain zero
answer: A null pointer compares unequal to every pointer to an object or function
questions.explanation: Null pointer semantics are defined by comparisons and conversion rules, not by a required all-zero representation.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between the null character and a null pointer?
options: The null character is a character value; a null pointer is a pointer value that designates no object or function
They are the same value and type
A null pointer terminates a C string
The null character can only appear in pointer objects
answer: The null character is a character value; a null pointer is a pointer value that designates no object or function
questions.explanation: The null character terminates strings. A null pointer is a special pointer value; the concepts have different types and uses.

questions.prompt: For char s[]="CS";, what storage does s contain?
options: C, S, and a terminating null character
A pointer to immutable literal storage
Only C and S with no terminator
The address of the literal as an integer
answer: C, S, and a terminating null character
questions.explanation: Array initialization copies the literal into a modifiable three-element char array including its terminator.

questions.prompt: A six-element int array uses the designated initializer {[3]=9} and has no other initializers. What is the sum of all its elements?
questions.explanation: The designated initializer sets only element 3 to 9. Every omitted element of the aggregate is zero-initialized, so the total sum is 9.

questions.prompt: Which statements about C strings are correct?
options: A string is terminated by a null character
strlen excludes the terminating null character
strcpy copies the terminating null character
Every char array is automatically a valid null-terminated string
answer: A string is terminated by a null character
strlen excludes the terminating null character
strcpy copies the terminating null character
questions.explanation: A C string is a character sequence ending at a null byte. strlen excludes that byte, while strcpy copies it to terminate the destination string.

questions.prompt: Which C17 expression-order statements are correct?
options: The left operand of && is evaluated before the right operand
The condition of ?: is evaluated before one selected branch
The operands of + have no specified left-to-right order
Arguments to a function are evaluated left to right
answer: The left operand of && is evaluated before the right operand
The condition of ?: is evaluated before one selected branch
The operands of + have no specified left-to-right order
questions.explanation: Logical AND and the conditional operator impose sequencing rules. Ordinary addition and function arguments do not have a general left-to-right evaluation order in C17.

questions.prompt: What can be concluded about the exact nonzero value returned by strcmp?
options: It is always the ASCII difference
It is the difference in string lengths
answer: Only its sign is specified
questions.explanation: strcmp specifies whether its result is negative, zero, or positive; the exact nonzero magnitude is not fixed.

questions.prompt: What is the behavior of printf("%d", 3.5) in a variadic call?
options: It prints the double bit pattern
A diagnostic is required in every implementation
answer: Undefined because %d expects an int
questions.explanation: Variadic arguments are not converted according to the format string. A double argument mismatched with %d has undefined behavior.

questions.prompt: An object pointer p is passed to printf with the %p conversion. Which argument form satisfies the required pointer type?
answer: (void *)p
questions.explanation: The %p conversion expects a void pointer argument. An object pointer can be converted to void * explicitly before passing it through the variadic argument list.

questions.prompt: What happens to a float argument in the unnamed portion of a variadic function call?
options: It is promoted to long double
answer: It is promoted to double
questions.explanation: The default argument promotions convert float to double for arguments corresponding to an ellipsis.

questions.prompt: Which is the safe pattern when realloc must preserve the old allocation if it fails?
options: Store the result in a temporary pointer and update the owner only on success
Assign the result directly to the only copy of p
answer: Store the result in a temporary pointer and update the owner only on success
questions.explanation: On failure realloc returns NULL and leaves the old allocation valid. A temporary pointer avoids losing the original address.

questions.prompt: What argument must be passed to free for a block returned by malloc?
options: The original allocation pointer or NULL
An interior pointer to its last byte
The first value stored in the block
Any pointer with the same numeric address after arithmetic
answer: The original allocation pointer or NULL
questions.explanation: free accepts the allocation pointer itself or NULL. Interior pointers and repeated frees are invalid.

questions.prompt: What does calloc guarantee about the bytes of a successful allocation?
options: They are all set to zero bits
Every pointer member is guaranteed to be a null pointer
Every floating member is guaranteed to equal 0.0
Each object is initialized by a constructor
answer: They are all set to zero bits
questions.explanation: calloc fills bytes with all-bits-zero; C does not require that representation to encode null pointers or floating zero for every type.

questions.prompt: Why is gets unsafe for reading input into a fixed-size array?
options: It has no parameter limiting how many bytes are stored
It always reads only one character
answer: It has no parameter limiting how many bytes are stored
questions.explanation: gets cannot enforce the destination bound and was removed from the C standard. fgets accepts an explicit size limit.

questions.prompt: For #define SQR(x) x*x, what does SQR(1+2) expand to and evaluate as?
answer: 1+2*1+2, which is 5
questions.explanation: Macro substitution is textual. Without parentheses the expansion is 1+2*1+2, which evaluates to 5 by operator precedence.

questions.prompt: Which definition protects a square macro from precedence errors?
answer: #define SQR(x) ((x) * (x))
questions.explanation: Parenthesizing each argument use and the complete expansion preserves grouping in surrounding expressions.

questions.prompt: What risk remains for SQR(i++) with a macro defined as ((x)*(x))?
options: The side effect can occur twice
The macro is converted to a function automatically
answer: The side effect can occur twice
questions.explanation: The argument text appears twice in the replacement, so i++ can be evaluated twice. Parentheses do not remove repeated side effects.

questions.prompt: What does typedef unsigned long Size; do?
options: Introduces Size as an alias for unsigned long
answer: Introduces Size as an alias for unsigned long
questions.explanation: typedef introduces a type name alias; it does not allocate storage or create a distinct representation by itself.

questions.prompt: In hosted C99 and later, what happens if main reaches its closing brace?
options: It is equivalent to returning zero
It returns the last local value
answer: It is equivalent to returning zero
questions.explanation: The standard gives main a special rule: reaching its closing brace returns zero. This rule does not apply to arbitrary non-void functions.

questions.prompt: Which return type is required for main in a hosted C program?
answer: int
questions.explanation: A hosted program defines main with return type int in one of the standard forms.

questions.prompt: What does the prototype int f(void); specify?
options: f takes no parameters and returns int
f accepts any number of parameters
answer: f takes no parameters and returns int
questions.explanation: The parameter list containing void explicitly specifies no parameters; the result type is int.

questions.prompt: A function returns the address of an automatic local variable. What is the problem after return?
options: The pointed-to object lifetime has ended
answer: The pointed-to object lifetime has ended
questions.explanation: An automatic local object ceases to exist when its block ends. Using the returned pointer to access it is invalid.

questions.prompt: What is guaranteed about the representation of a null object pointer?
options: It need not consist of all zero bits
It is always all zero bits
It has the same representation as the null character
answer: It need not consist of all zero bits
questions.explanation: C specifies null-pointer value semantics, not a required bit pattern.

questions.prompt: What values can standard C _Bool store?
answer: 0 or 1
questions.explanation: Conversion to _Bool produces zero if the value compares equal to zero and one otherwise.

questions.prompt: Which declaration makes f a function taking no parameters and returning a pointer to int?
answer: int *f(void);
questions.explanation: The declarator is a function named f with a void parameter list; its return type is int pointer. Parentheses around *f would instead make f a function pointer object.

questions.prompt: What does sizeof applied to a function designator do in standard C?
options: It is not permitted for a function type
It returns a function pointer size
answer: It is not permitted for a function type
questions.explanation: sizeof cannot be applied to function types. A pointer to function is a distinct object type and can be measured.

questions.prompt: For enum E {A=3, B, C=10, D}; what value does D have?
questions.explanation: An enumerator without an explicit value follows its predecessor by one. C is 10, so D is 11.

questions.prompt: Why can a program not apply unary & to a bit-field member?
options: A bit-field is not an independently addressable object
A bit-field is always a pointer
The operator is valid only on arrays
answer: A bit-field is not an independently addressable object
questions.explanation: C prohibits taking a bit-field address because the field may not occupy an independently addressable object.

questions.prompt: Which statements about C storage duration and linkage are correct?
options: A block-scope static object retains its value between calls
A file-scope static function has internal linkage
An ordinary automatic local object ends its lifetime at block exit
extern always defines a new object
answer: A block-scope static object retains its value between calls
A file-scope static function has internal linkage
An ordinary automatic local object ends its lifetime at block exit
questions.explanation: Static duration preserves a local static value. File-scope static restricts linkage; ordinary locals end at block exit. extern alone does not define storage.

questions.prompt: Which statements about malloc and realloc are correct?
options: malloc returns suitably aligned storage for object types
A failed nonzero-size realloc leaves the original allocation valid
free sets the caller pointer to NULL
realloc accepts an interior pointer to a block
answer: malloc returns suitably aligned storage for object types
A failed nonzero-size realloc leaves the original allocation valid
questions.explanation: malloc returns suitably aligned storage. If a nonzero realloc request fails, the old block remains allocated; free does not overwrite the caller pointer.

questions.prompt: What does the declaration const int *p prevent?
options: Modifying the pointed-to int through p
answer: Modifying the pointed-to int through p
questions.explanation: The pointed-to type is const-qualified through p, so writes through it are disallowed; p itself may be reassigned.

questions.prompt: Which statement about errno after a successful library call is correct?
options: The function is not generally required to clear errno on success
It is guaranteed to be zero
It always equals the return value
It cannot be changed by a library function
answer: The function is not generally required to clear errno on success
questions.explanation: A function may leave errno unchanged after success. Inspect it only according to that function's documented error convention.

questions.prompt: Which expressions have defined sequencing between their relevant evaluations?
options: The left-to-right short-circuit evaluation of a && b
The two operands of i++ + i
Function arguments are guaranteed left to right
answer: The comma expression (i++, i+1)
The left-to-right short-circuit evaluation of a && b
questions.explanation: The comma operator sequences its left operand before the right; && sequences left before right. Addition and function arguments have no general left-to-right order.
